name: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
problem: Mamba-1's selective scan was correct but ran as a slow sequential recurrence with a small state (d_state=16), so it lost to attention on recall tasks and its kernel could not use tensor cores effectively.
mechanism: Establishes state space duality (SSD): a large class of structured matrices are semiseparable and can be decomposed either as an SSM recurrence or as an attention-like sum, so SSMs and attention variants are two views of the same object rather than competing families. Exploiting this yields Mamba-2, whose core layer is a refinement of the Mamba selective SSM in two ways that matter for hardware. (1) It moves to a much larger state, d_state=128 instead of 16, grouped into heads, which is what recovers recall. (2) It replaces the scalar-per-head recurrence with a matrix recurrence expressible as a single SSD algorithm: within a chunk compute the attention-like form, across chunks apply the semiseparable decay matrix. This turns the scan into block-parallel matmuls that DO map onto tensor cores, so the sequential-scan bottleneck is largely removed. State remains fixed-size per layer (batch, n_heads, head_dim, d_state), so as with Mamba-1 there is still no KV cache and still no length-dependent decode memory growth.
speedup_reported: The Mamba-2 core layer is 2-8x faster than the Mamba-1 selective SSM while remaining a drop-in replacement and remaining competitive on upstream tasks. Measured on A100 GPUs against the authors' own Mamba-1 reference implementation. This is a kernel-level statement about one layer, not an end-to-end model throughput number, and the 2-8x range is wide because it varies with sequence length and batch size.
notes: ICML 2024; venue per the arXiv comment field (no journal-ref on the abs page). The SSD insight is what makes SSM training hardware-coherent rather than a sequential-loop curiosity, and it is the reason Mamba-2 kernel work (vLLM's 'SSD' CI job, llama.cpp's Mamba-2 Metal scan optimization) exists at all. Engine support verified: vLLM has native Mamba2ForCausalLM; llama.cpp has LLM_ARCH_MAMBA2 inside llm_arch_is_recurrent().
